static_traits.name: Chen Zeyu
static_traits.family_status: Living with a French bulldog; not yet living with parents
static_traits.social_status: Has several friends to talk to, but has not yet opened up to them about feeling 'seen as useless'; relationships with friends damaged by feeling seen as useless
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar problems before; no prior psychotherapy or counseling experience
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and automatic thoughts concretely; negative tone, marked self-denial; acceptable cooperativeness but skeptical of intervention; thinking tendencies such as catastrophizing, mind reading, and personalization

basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt my friends think I am useless, because I am unemployed and live off a trust fund.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of being seen as useless have affected my self-worth and cause distress in social situations, so I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: A few months ago, feelings of 'being seen as useless by friends' began after losing work; worsening over time, especially when seeing friends' career success; tried distracting with manicures and expensive red wine, but to no avail.

After failing the driving test, intense feelings of incompetence and anxiety emerged; whenever thinking of driving or seeing others drive effortlessly, thoughts like 'I will never learn' and 'I will crash' appear, avoiding driving-related situations; even practicing with spousal support, heart racing and difficulty concentrating.

core_beliefs: I am incompetent, someone who cannot do things well

special_situations.event: Gathers with friends and sees them making progress in their careers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my achievements are not like my peers', it equals failure and worthlessness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces talking about recent life in front of friends, avoids opening up; numbs emotions through manicures and expensive red wine
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am terrible.

special_situations.event: Thinking of being unemployed and dependent on a trust fund at social gatherings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have no work or income, others will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding expressing true feelings to friends; reducing social exposure to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am useless inside, thinking I am someone living off a trust fund.

special_situations.event: When sitting in the car getting ready to practice driving
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make another mistake, it proves I will never learn to drive
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding practicing driving, having others drive instead, or avoiding outings involving driving
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will lose control / crash; I will never learn.

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others can do it easily but I cannot, it means something is wrong with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing practice; displacing attention to reduce the sense of frustration
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I definitely cannot learn; this shows something is wrong with me.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted by friends and significant others, and to be seen as valuable and competent
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being belittled and rejected; being seen as useless or forever incompetent
defense_goal: Lowering shame and anxiety by avoiding socializing and driving situations
Attributes negative evaluations to others' thoughts to protect self-esteem
Temporarily alleviating pain by displacing attention through material consumption

object_relations.self_representation: Incompetent, a failure lagging behind in comparison
object_relations.object_representation: Picky, judgmental, and more successful others / friends

object_relations.self_representation: A learner driver / failure who may err at any moment
object_relations.object_representation: A harshly judging examiner or bystander

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing friends' views of oneself or being mentioned in social settings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others will belittle oneself like judges (transference: projecting self-denial as others' views)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Asserting 'they look down on me' in a certain tone, ignoring verification and contrary evidence, with a firm tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests trying new cognitive-behavioral methods or behavioral experiments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treating past failure experiences as evidence, presuming this time will not work either
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'I tried changing my mind before and it was useless' in a rational tone, thereby politely declining deeper attempts.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to practice driving again or recalling the exam failure experience
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning outward frustration and anger toward oneself, labeling oneself as 'incompetent/stupid'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming expressions (e.g., 'I am an idiot'), in a depressed tone, lowering self-worth.

manifestations: Worrying friends think one is useless and thus not daring to open up to them
Feeling alienated due to comparison at social gatherings
Shaken sense of self-worth after unemployment and dependence on a trust fund
Tightly binding ability with social evaluation/employment
outcomes: Avoidance behaviors and persistent negative emotions

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Constantly speculating about others' negative evaluations of oneself in social settings
Frequently using self-blaming language (e.g., 'I am not capable')

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Being convinced of mind-reading inferences like 'friends think I am useless' and 'everyone will think I am a fool'

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not having opened up true feelings to friends
Pushes back the urge to seek support and chooses to bear it alone

positive_force: Spouse provides practical support and practice partnership
Has a few close friends who can potentially provide support
Willing to seek professional help and try new methods (despite skepticism)
Usually able to cope well in other life areas (no similar feelings of incompetence before)
negative_force: Tends toward cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, mind reading, personalization, and overgeneralization
Self-worth excessively dependent on external evaluation and career achievements
Avoiding socializing and driving maintains anxiety
Ongoing social comparison after unemployment aggravates shame and anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: Fear of and avoidance of driving
antecedent: Getting into the car to practice driving
When thinking about or discussing retaking the exam / driving practice
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and overgeneralizing cognition formed from failing the test (one failure means 'never learning', associating with 'crashing')
target_behavior.function: Escaping fear and potential failure to avoid shame and anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Travel restricted, life radius shrunk; relationship with spouse under strain; persistent maintenance of fear of driving

target_behavior.behavior: Withdrawal and self-deprecation in social situations (mind-reading style self-monitoring)
antecedent: When talking about work and income
target_behavior.core_reason: Strongly ties self-worth to employment/income and engages in mind reading and personalization, presuming others will belittle her
target_behavior.function: Escaping the possibility of negative evaluation and shame; short-term relief of anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Relationships with friends are damaged, self-worth further declines, negative emotions persist
